doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: Comparing Henry and George Brunies on trombone
summary: Sbarbaro compares Henry and George Brunies; Henry took lessons.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: by the way, you're not going to hurt George's feelings by answering this because... Who's George? I mean, George Brunas' feelings, but how did George compare with Henny?
I don't think any... I don't think George played as good as Henry, but George is still a terrific trombone player.
That's what George says. George says that himself. His brother is... Henry,

Henry had an awful lot of stuff. I think Henry today playing trombone on the street, then, playing like he played then right today would be a sensation. Henry played. I was in Chicago just a couple years ago and I was with George Brunas' feelings every night, you know? And he's playing fine. He's playing real good. Oh, Henry, Henry was a good trombone. But you see, you're going to go into that same old argument again. He wasn't a school musician like Edwards was.
You understand? He wasn't what you call a real hot man. No, he had a lot of stuff. He had good execution and all, you know? And he'd blow his head off. He took lessons from Dave Poikins.
Henry took lessons. I like me.
